title: Lindsay Clancy's push to probe holdout juror hits snag before pivotal retrial hearing
summary: Lindsay Clancy returns to court in person as her defense pushes a double jeopardy motion and seeks to investigate holdout juror Michael Desronvil.
story: Edward Paltzik, attorney for the lone holdout juror, reacts to Lindsay Clancy defense attorney Kevin Reddington's motion to investigate his client, calling it a direct attack on the Constitution. The 'Outnumbered' panel warns against setting a dangerous precedent by targeting jurors.

PLYMOUTH, Mass. — A Massachusetts judge overseeing the Lindsay Clancy case is expected to hear arguments on her double jeopardy motion Tuesday, while another push to investigate the lone holdout juror in her mistrial may be on hold — for now.
Clancy is expected in court in person for the first time since her trial ended in a deadlocked jury and the judge declared a mistrial on Sept. 4.

In the weeks since her mistrial, Clancy's case has remained a topic of national interest, with fellow jurors and Clancy's defense attorney attacking the lone holdout. At the same time, Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz's office has been relatively quiet about their plans for a potential retrial.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ASKS FOR ONE THING IN NEW VIDEO AFTER MISTRIAL DRAMA
Lindsay Clancy in court last month. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)
LINDSAY CLANCY'S PUSH TO INVESTIGATE HOLDOUT JUROR COULD BE PAUSED AS DEFENSE, PROSECUTORS AGREE TO ADJOURN
Here's a roundup of what to expect as she returns to court:

Clancy's defense lawyer Kevin Reddington had called for an inquiry into the lone holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, whom he has dubbed "the obstructionist juror." Desronvil opposed 11 others on the panel and was the only one who wanted to find her guilty until the end.
Michael Desronvil, who is said to be hiding out at an undisclosed location, spoke out publicly for the first time in a video exclusively shared with Fox News' "Hannity" Monday evening.

"I know the whole focus has been on me, but we want to reel everything back and put the focus on the three angels," he said. "The ones that can't speak for themselves, the ones that can't defend themselves, and the ones that can't fight the battles — and those are Cora, Dawson and Callan."
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR'S LAWYER TORCHES 'LOONEY TUNES MOTION' TO INVESTIGATE HIM

According to Desronvil's attorney, Edward Paltzik, both Reddington and Plymouth County prosecutors agreed to adjourn that motion after counsel for the holdout raised an objection because they didn't yet have access to impounded materials necessary to file a response.
"The DA and Reddington consent to adjourn the motion to investigate Michael," Paltzik told Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Monday.
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
ATTORNEY FOR LONE HOLDOUT JUROR IN LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL PUSHES BACK ON CLAIMS OF REFUSING THE LAW
"If Judge Sullivan signs an order today, much of it could be adjourned," he said. "Either way, a status conference is still likely."

Reddington pushed back, forcefully, while conceding that he and the district attorney's office had agreed to continue the motion out of professional courtesy to local counsel now representing the juror.
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON FIRES BACK AT LONE HOLDOUT JUROR'S ATTORNEY AFTER FIERY INTERVIEW
Defense attorney Kevin Reddington addresses reporters as jurors weigh the case against Lindsay Clancy in the 2023 deaths of her three children. (Photo by JOSEPH PREZIOSO / AFP via Getty Images)

"Earlier today, both the government and I were contacted by a professional local attorney who represents Juror Doe," he said, not using the juror's name due to an impoundment order from the court. "That attorney requested — as any qualified counsel would — adequate time to review our motion and reply."

He added, "As is professional courtesy, both the government and I agreed to continue this specific motion to a later date at their request. The motion remains active, fully alive, and is currently pending a ruling from Judge Sullivan. We will not allow a publicity-seeking opportunist to twist simple courtroom courtesy into a victory that does not exist."
The terms adjourned and continued are similar but have distinct meanings.
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. (Fugitive TV)

"Adjournment generally signifies that something like a hearing is off indefinitely especially because no date is specified," explained retired Massachusetts Judge Carol Erskine. "A continuance is a simple request by a party or two parties to get a new date. [Reddington] objects because adjournment is a misrepresentation of what is happening."
CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR TAPS FORMER TRUMP LAWYER TO FIGHT BACK AS HE’S ‘DRAGGED THROUGH THE MUD’: ATTORNEY
District Attorney Timothy Cruz leaves Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Thursday, September, 3, 2026.  (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
If Reddington ultimately prevails, the court could hold a Fidler hearing, where the judge would question Desronvil.

"There are three phases to a hearing like that," said Erskine, who is also a child welfare advocate and has been closely following the case. "This is something that could result in a strong manifest necessity claim but hard to tell until it happens."
LINDSAY CLANCY'S ATTORNEY ASKS JUDGE TO ACQUIT HER OUTRIGHT, ENDING CASE AND BARRING A RETRIAL

Judge William Sullivan, left, delivered a rare Tuey-Rodriguez charge to the deadlocked jury as Lindsay Clancy, right, looked on during proceedings in Plymouth Superior Court. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool and David L. Ryan/Pool)
Manifest necessity is the legal standard required to hold a second trial. Erskine said the motion is a long-shot but Reddington is likely laying the foundation for an appeal in the future.

"The big issue, in my opinion, is whether outside information came into the jury room and whether a judge can find that any 'hypothetical juror' would let it influence his decision," she told Fox News Digital. "It’s definitely more complicated than that, but there is case law about it."

"This is a strange new world in which disagreeing jurors and their surrogates conduct a public debate after the trial in the media and social media," said Jack Lu, another retired Massachusetts judge.

Lindsay Clancy looks at jurors as Judge Sullivan asks them to start deliberations for a sixth day during her murder trial on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Plymouth, Mass. (Pool Photo by Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger)

Reddington's request for an inquiry into Desronvil is largely based on allegations from other jurors who accused him of having reasonable doubt about the case and ignoring it. He is seeking phone records, his confidential juror questionnaire and police records.
However, he's also called him an "obstructionist" outside the courtroom and accused him of having an "agenda."

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse on Sept. 4, the day the mistrial was declared.
Still, he downplayed speculation from legal analysts about a potential defamation lawsuit from the holdout against Clancy's team.
Patrick Clancy on the stand at Lindsay Clancy's murder trial on July 29, 2026. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
"Defamation law is textbook complex," he told Fox News Digital. "Statements made in court proceedings are privileged."
Statements made out of court that could appear to be "false statements of fact" may end up being considered opinions, he added.

"If a person says X happened, and we all know that person was not present, then it may be deemed to be an opinion," he said. "This might apply to any alleged statements about what happened in the jury room."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Patrick Clancy and Rachel Danis hold hands as they walk through East Midtown in New York City, NY, Wedensday, September 2, 2026. (Elder Ordonez/InStar for Fox News Digital)

"I don’t think any of the legal maneuvering, double jeopardy, all that stuff, a hearing in the trial court with the juror, I don't think it’s going anywhere," said Mark Bederow, a New York-based criminal defense attorney and former prosecutor who is following the case.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
"If you get down to brass tacks, once you get through all this, now you have to look at the DA and say, what are you doing?" he added.
Most prosecutors would not seek a second trial in a case where only one juror agreed with them, he said, but that appears unlikely in this case.
GOT A TIP?

"At the first trial, the prosecution, in my view, failed miserably to satisfy their burden — but there is a credible argument that she's guilty and intended to cause their deaths and knew right from wrong," he said. "In order for them to win, they need to get better experts."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST
The Commonwealth needs experts who can discredit Clancy's defense experts, he said. And prosecutors also have room to improve their jury selection.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
As for Reddington, he described him as "a titan of the Massachusetts bar" who is filing motions that make sense for his client's benefit, regardless of his commentary outside the courtroom.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"That's not frivolous, and any lawyer knows that," he told Fox News Digital.

A routine traffic stop on a Kentucky interstate turned deadly Monday when a state trooper was gunned down, launching a statewide manhunt that ended with a suspect in custody.
Trooper Hayden Phillips, 30, was killed along Interstate 65 in Warren County. He leaves behind a wife and three young sons.

"He was senselessly murdered," U.S. Attorney Kyle Bumgarner said at a Monday night news conference. "We have a wife that expected her husband to come home. We have three little boys who don’t have a dad."
SUSPECTS AT LARGE AFTER TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT KILLED, PIMA COUNTY CORRECTIONS OFFICER WOUNDED IN SHOOTING
Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips was killed while patrolling Interstate 65 in Warren County on Monday. (KY State Police)
Phillips was a three-year veteran of Kentucky State Police, assigned to Post 3 in Bowling Green. He graduated from Cadet Class 103 and was known to fellow troopers as Unit 369.
"Because he served us, because he served our community, because he wanted to keep each of us safe," Bumgarner said. "He gave the ultimate sacrifice."
Kentucky State Police Commissioner Col. Phillip Burnett Jr. pledged to pursue justice for Phillips.
"We will seek justice for Hayden," Burnett said. "Let me repeat that, we will seek justice for Hayden. We will not rest until this happens."
JURY CONVICTS KEVIN SALAZAR IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLING OF LA DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER
Burnett called Phillips’ death one of the most difficult moments the agency could endure.

"His dedication to duty and commitment to the Commonwealth will never be forgotten," Burnett said. "Our hearts break for Trooper Phillips’ family, loved ones and fellow troopers as we grieve this tremendous loss."

State police initially announced a trooper-involved shooting on northbound I-65 near the 38-mile marker. They then asked the public to watch for a bluish-gray Honda Civic with an Alabama tag that had been present during the shooting. A Blue Alert identified Emonnie Branch as the wanted person.
Kentucky State Police released an image of a Honda Civic they said was present during the shooting of Trooper Hayden Phillips on Interstate 65. (KY State Police)

Louisville Metro Police took Branch into custody, and state police canceled the alert. Burnett said Branch was being charged with the murder of a first responder. Bumgarner said Branch would be returned to Warren County to face state murder charges.
MAN WANTED IN DEPUTY AMBUSH CAUGHT AFTER WILDLIFE CAMERA SIGHTING AND MAJOR MANHUNT
A Kentucky State Police cruiser vehicle is shown in this undated photo. (Silas Walker/Lexington Herald-Leader/Tribune News Service)
"I want you to know I only mentioned his name one time," Burnett said of Branch, condemning what he called the suspect’s "cowardly actions."
Authorities have not said why Phillips stopped the vehicle or whether Branch had a prior criminal record.

"One of our own was gunned down and murdered on the side of the road," Bumgarner said. He pledged that the Justice Department would give Kentucky prosecutors and investigators "every tool" and "every bit of support" it could provide.
Burnett addressed Phillips’ family directly, promising that state police would stand beside them.
"You will not walk this path alone," he said.
"Rest Easy U/369. We have it from here," state police wrote in a tribute to Phillips.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND
Gov. Andy Beshear called Phillips a hero who dedicated himself to protecting Kentucky. He said the trooper was also "a devoted husband and loving father to three children."
"Let us wrap our arms around this family during this unimaginable time," the governor wrote.

Rep. Brett Guthrie, R-Ky., thanked law enforcement for its swift work and said Phillips’ wife, their three young children and his colleagues were in his prayers. Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., urged people to pray for Phillips’ family and fellow officers.
Rep. Morgan McGarvey, D-Ky., also offered prayers for Phillips’ family and said Kentucky would not forget his service.
"Alongside his fellow KSP troopers and all who knew and loved him, we will not forget his service to our commonwealth," McGarvey wrote.

Country singer Lee Greenwood mourned Phillips, writing that he and his wife, Kim, had learned of the trooper’s death and would "always stand with the men and women in blue."

title: Grandmother sues after alleged AI facial recognition error led to months in jail, experts sound alarm
summary: Angela Lipps was arrested at gunpoint and jailed for nearly six months after Fargo police allegedly relied on an uncorroborated AI facial recognition match.
story: In an interview with Fox News Digital, a policing tech expert said officers have wrongfully arrested 16 people after alleged facial recognition mistakes, warning agencies need stronger safeguards as AI becomes more common in investigations.

A Tennessee grandmother has filed a lawsuit against a North Dakota city and police department, accusing officials of wrongfully detaining her for nearly six months after allegedly misusing artificial intelligence facial recognition technology to investigate a bank theft case.
Angela Lipps, now 50, of Elizabethton, Tennessee, said she was caring for her neighbor's four young children when police showed up at the home and arrested her at gunpoint in July 2025.

The complaint, filed Sept. 15, 2026, alleges that authorities relied exclusively on a flawed AI facial recognition match to extradite Lipps from Tennessee to North Dakota, despite her having no connection to the crime or the state.
Experts on police technology told Fox News Digital that the case is among more than a dozen known instances involving alleged police mishandling of facial recognition technology.
"I sat in a county jail in Tennessee for 108 days," Lipps said in a GoFundMe post. "They said I was fugitive from justice. I had no bail. No one interviewed me. I just sat and waited."
FRAUD EXPERT WARNS AI IS HELPING CRIMINALS OUTPACE THE GOVERNMENT: 'DON'T HAVE THE RIGHT TOOLS'
Lipps says she spent 108 days in a Tennessee jail before being extradited to North Dakota and eventually cleared. (City of Fargo/GoFundMe)

The bank theft case stemmed from April and May 2025, when an unknown woman allegedly used fake IDs and stolen identities to perpetrate bank fraud in Fargo and West Fargo, North Dakota, according to the lawsuit.
Officials then used a photo from a fraudulent ID card presented by the suspect, rather than surveillance footage, to conduct facial recognition searches using Clearview AI, plaintiffs alleged.

While Clearview AI explicitly requires facial recognition matches to be treated as potential leads, Fargo police allegedly characterized the AI match as a positive identification without disclosing that it had not been independently corroborated, according to the complaint.
Meanwhile, the West Fargo Police Department reportedly declined to seek charges because the AI match was uncorroborated.
A West Fargo police captain reportedly characterized AI facial recognition as "close to a last-ditch effort" in police investigations, the lawsuit said.
FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES
Angela Lipps says police overlooked evidence that she was hundreds of miles away when the North Dakota bank thefts occurred. (City of Fargo/GoFundMe)

According to the complaint, Detective Lucas Heck did not review Lipps’ financial or travel records that showed she was in Tennessee during the bank thefts and failed to conduct photo lineups with bank tellers. Surveillance video reportedly showed physical differences between Lipps and the suspect, including a different build and a neck tattoo on Lipps that was absent from the suspect.
"Heck ignored, concealed, and misrepresented exculpatory evidence that Lipps did not commit the bank thefts," the complaint alleged.
On July 14, 2025, U.S. Marshals surrounded a neighbor’s house in Tennessee and arrested Lipps at gunpoint on a nationwide warrant, plaintiffs said.
Lipps was extradited to North Dakota and reportedly held on a $100,000 bond while facing eight felony counts, the most severe of which carried maximum sentences of up to 10 years in prison.
Prosecutors dismissed all charges on Dec. 24, 2025, after Lipps produced bank records showing that she was in Tennessee when the bank thefts occurred, plaintiffs said.
"When she was released, she found that her residence, car, and personal property were lost while she was absent," the complaint said.
FLOCK SAFETY CEO CALLS FOR NATIONAL 'COMPROMISE' AMID CAMERA SABOTAGE AND PUBLIC REVOLT
Fargo officials later acknowledged investigative errors involving the department's use of facial recognition technology. (City of Fargo/GoFundMe)
Following public scrutiny, the Fargo Police Department and city of Fargo acknowledged at a March 2026 press conference that the department had made investigative errors.
"When chief found some errors that were made in this area of where we got our facial recognition and how that worked, we immediately addressed it," Mayor Tim Mahoney said.

Clare Garvie, the deputy director of Technology Law & Policy with the Policing Project, told Fox News Digital that incidents involving the alleged mishandling of AI have increased as law enforcement agencies adjust to "integrate AI and additional tools into police investigations."

"We are aware of 16 misidentifications stemming from a face recognition match where someone was wrongfully arrested and spent time in jail because of that misidentification, and in many of these cases, it was because additional investigative steps weren't taken to prove, or in these cases to disprove, the face recognition match," Garvie said in an interview.
"We're asking officers to do a different job now, such that we need to update how we think about these workflows," she added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Nate Freed-Wessler, a deputy director at the American Civil Liberties Union, said the rise of artificial intelligence in law enforcement has fueled wrongful arrests across the country.
"We've been seeing these kinds of wrongful arrests happening for at least five or six years now out of this kind of AI technology. And the rate of them seems to be increasing," he said.
"We've seen cases where police intentionally avoid making any notes about their use of facial recognition technology or other AI."
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Lindsay Clancy's 'Shooter McGavin' unloads on 'hoodie-wearing lawyer' amid war of words over holdout juror
summary: Kevin Reddington's motion to investigate holdout juror Michael Desronvil in the Lindsay Clancy mistrial may not be on the agenda at key status conference Tuesday.
story: ‘Outnumbered’ co-host Kayleigh McEnany discusses comments from Edward Paltzik, the attorney for Lindsay Clancy holdout juror Michael Desronvil, and details about a pivotal motion in the upcoming hearing on ‘The Story.’

PLYMOUTH, Mass. — Lindsay Clancy's legal team and Massachusetts prosecutors have agreed to delay defense attorney Kevin Reddington’s motion to investigate the lone holdout juror in her mistrial, his attorney Edward Paltzik told Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Monday.

"The DA and Reddington consent to adjourn the motion to investigate Michael," Paltzik said. "If Judge Sullivan signs an order today, much of it could be adjourned. Either way, a status conference is still likely. But the motion about Michael is likely not on tomorrow."

Clancy attorney Kevin Reddington, however, fired back a short time later in a fiery statement of his own, calling Paltzik's statement "pure nonsense" while conceding that he and county prosecutors had agreed to a continuation as a "professional courtesy" to local counsel now working with the holdout juror.

A final decision is subject to Judge William Sullivan, but the judge has not yet announced a decision one way or the other. The delay agreement comes as the juror's new local counsel informed the parties that he does not have access to impounded information necessary to prepare a response.
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON FIRES BACK AT LONE HOLDOUT JUROR'S ATTORNEY AFTER FIERY INTERVIEW

Michael P. Desronvil, left, the lone holdout juror who forced a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case, has retained an attorney who once represented President Donald Trump. Clancy, right, faced three counts of first-degree murder in the strangling deaths of her three children. (Facebook/Brittany K and Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

"Earlier today, both the government and I were contacted by a professional local attorney who represents Juror Doe," Reddington said, not naming Desronvil due to an impoundment order from the court. "That attorney requested — as any qualified counsel would — adequate time to review our motion and reply. As is professional courtesy, both the government and I agreed to continue this specific motion to a later date at their request."
He said the motion "remains active, fully alive, and is currently pending a ruling."
"We will not allow a publicity-seeking opportunist to twist simple courtroom courtesy into a victory that does not exist," he added.
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. (Fugitive TV)
The terms adjourned and continued are similar but have distinct meanings.

"Adjournment generally signifies that something like a hearing is off indefinitely especially because no date is specified," explained retired Massachusetts Judge Carol Erskine. "A continuance is a simple request by a party or two parties to get a new date. [Reddington] objects because adjournment is a misrepresentation of what is happening."
Callan, left, Dawson and Cora Clancy. The three children were killed at their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. (Lindsay Marie Clancy/Facebook)
Clancy is due in court at 9 a.m. Tuesday for a status conference in the wake of her mistrial — her first court date since jurors deadlocked on Sept. 4.
"We have our local counsel showing up either way," Paltzik said. "It’s important to note that all of this is subject to the Judge’s discretion."

The hearing was expected to cover Reddington's motion to hold an inquiry into the holdout, Michael Desronvil, as well as a double jeopardy motion seeking to dismiss the charges instead of holding a retrial.

Prosecutors are also expected to give an update on their plans.

Reddington had asked the court for an investigation into Desronvil, the only juror out of 12 who maintained that Clancy is guilty of murder in the strangling deaths of her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

"I just learned that Kevin ‘Shooter McGavin’ Reddington HAD multiple peremptory challenges remaining when the opportunity to strike Michael came around," he wrote on X Monday, in a reference to a character from the movie "Happy Gilmore."

title: Vape store arrests near Ole Miss campus not believed to be linked to two student deaths, state official says
summary: Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell said the two arrests near the Ole Miss campus are not believed to be tied to the deaths of two students.
story: Mississippi Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell discusses the ongoing investigation into the deaths of two Ole Miss students as safety concerns grow over the herbal supplement kratom.

FIRST ON FOX: OXFORD, Miss. – Three people facing charges related to a vape and tobacco store near the University of Mississippi are not believed to be connected to the deaths of two Ole Miss students, an official told Fox News Digital.

Mississippi Department of Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell told Fox News Digital the arrests of Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Mohamed, 18, aren't connected to the deaths of Ole Miss students Aidan Hamilton, 18, and Robert Strang, 20. Amer Alowdi, 40, who owns the Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store in Oxford, was indicted in 2022 and fled the country before he could face formal prosecution, documents allege.

"I don't think there's a direct relation to this particular case," Tindell said. "Based upon what's happened in this particular case, in this situation, there's going to be some enhanced efforts in and around Oxford as it relates to anybody that's trying to sell these products or other products that would be unlawful."

He said autopsies into the deaths of Strang and Hamilton are completed, and said the state's medical examiner is writing the toxicology report, which will be shared with the Lafayette County Coroner "very soon."

Court documents uncovered by Fox News Digital also revealed the owner of the vape shop near the Ole Miss campus was previously indicted for trafficking hundreds of doses of an illegal synthetic cannabinoid.

title: WATCH: ‘American Idol’ alum Caleb Flynn tells cops flag-carrying stranger came to door before wife’s shooting
summary: Both sides rested in Caleb Flynn's Ohio murder trial Monday, setting the stage for closing arguments in the killing of his wife, Ashley Flynn.
story: Fox News contributor James Gagliano discusses new testimony in former 'American Idol' contestant Caleb Flynn's murder trial on 'America Reports.'
Both sides rested Monday in the Ohio murder trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn, setting the stage for closing arguments Tuesday before the case is handed to jurors.

Prosecutors rested after more than a week of testimony in the killing of Flynn's wife, Ashley Flynn. The defense then rested without calling any witnesses. Judge Jeannine N. Pratt dismissed jurors for the day and said closing arguments will begin Tuesday morning.

Flynn has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges. Prosecutors allege he shot Ashley in the back of the head inside their Tipp City home Feb. 16 before staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in.
DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER

"It's not unusual for the defense to not present a case," Paul Mauro, a former NYPD inspector and Fox News contributor, told Fox News Digital. "Remember, the burden of proof resides with the prosecution."
Caleb Flynn speaks with investigators during a recorded police interview following the Feb. 16, 2026, shooting death of his wife, Ashley Flynn. (WKEF)
"If the defense feels it has poked enough holes in the prosecution, they can emphasize that in their closing argument, and lean on the fact that there are holes in the case," Mauro said.
Mauro expects Flynn's attorneys to focus heavily on the circumstantial nature of the case and argue investigators settled on Flynn too quickly.

"There are no witnesses, no video, no murder weapon," Mauro said. "The close will focus on the idea that the police and prosecution rushed to judgment, settled quickly on Caleb, then found facts that they felt would support their case."
Mauro said there could be another strategic benefit to the defense resting without calling witnesses.
"Another aspect of the defense not putting on a case: it doesn't draw attention to the fact that Caleb himself never takes the stand in his own defense," he said.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The prosecution also ended its case without calling the couple's 10- and 12-year-old daughters, who were inside the home when their mother was killed. Their potential testimony had remained a possibility as late as Monday morning.
During a police interview played for jurors Monday, Flynn referenced one of his daughters while describing a stranger he said appeared at the family’s home the day before Ashley was killed.
Flynn said Ashley and their daughters were in the living room when a car pulled up and sat outside before a man with long hair got out and approached the front porch.
"My daughter can confirm," Flynn told investigators.
MISTRESS SAYS SHE GAVE ‘AMERICAN IDOL’ CONTESTANT ULTIMATUM BEFORE WIFE’S KILLING BLEW UP AFFAIR
Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (WKEF)
Flynn described the man as awkward, with no company logo visible on his clothing, and said he gave Ashley what Flynn described as a "weird" pitch involving an American flag.
Flynn said Ashley eventually closed the door after the man indicated he would return later.

The state's final day of testimony gave jurors competing timelines of the hours before Ashley's death – one based on Flynn's statements to police and another built from digital evidence recovered from his devices.
Ohio BCI criminal intelligence analyst Samantha Reeb also walked jurors through Flynn's account of the night Ashley was killed and compared it with data recovered from his devices.

Flynn told police he fell asleep beside his youngest daughter before gunshots woke him. He said he froze for several seconds, ran to the master bedroom and found Ashley unresponsive before calling 911 roughly two to five minutes later.
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

Reeb testified Flynn's Apple Watch recorded several bursts of movement between 1:19 and 1:56 a.m. At 2:17 a.m., his AirPods connected as an audio source before his watch logged another 105 steps over the next 10 minutes.
Alleigha Botner wipes away tears while testifying about messages exchanged with Caleb Flynn, during his murder trial in Ohio. (WKEF)
His iPhone also switched eight times between the AirPods and speaker before Flynn unlocked the phone and called 911 around 2:30 a.m.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
Reeb also pointed to location data that did not match a message Flynn sent Alleigha Botner, Flynn's mistress, the day before Ashley was killed.
SEND US A TIP
Flynn told Botner he had gone to Ashley's parents' home as he prepared to tell them he planned to leave their daughter.
"Went to their house and no one was there," Flynn wrote. "Stayed a little while and nothing."
But Reeb testified investigators recovered 5,162 location points from Flynn's device during that period, with none placing it near Ashley's parents' home.
Ashley Flynn, a Tipp City Schools substitute teacher and volleyball coach, was found dead in her Ohio home on Feb. 16, 2026. (Tipp City Schools)
GOT A TIP?
"There's no location data in the area of the Smith residence," Reeb testified.
The trial also included two days of testimony from Botner, who detailed their affair and read messages exchanged in the months before Ashley's death.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Botner testified Flynn repeatedly talked about wanting his wife dead, including one message in which he allegedly said he stayed up until 4 a.m. "literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."

But Flynn’s attorneys used their cross-examination to emphasize the broader context of more than 107,000 messages exchanged during the roughly year-and-a-half affair, including emotionally charged language used by Botner herself.
Botner also testified she understood Flynn’s plans for Feb. 16 to mean he intended to finally leave Ashley and seek a divorce – not kill her.
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Shortly after midnight that morning, however, Flynn allegedly told Botner, "It’s happening," followed by, "February 16th – day I’ll never forget."
"You’re about to be free," Botner responded.
"I choose you," Flynn replied.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Investigators have not recovered the gun prosecutors allege was used to kill Ashley despite extensive searches. There was no eyewitness to the shooting, and testimony showed no gunshot residue was found on Flynn.
With both sides finished presenting evidence, jurors will return Tuesday morning for closing arguments and instructions from the judge before beginning deliberations.
Fox News Digital has remained in contact with Flynn's attorney, who declined to comment while the trial is ongoing.

title: Attorney for lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy mistrial pushes back on claims of refusing the law
summary: Lindsay Clancy's holdout juror had "zero doubt" about his position, his attorney tells Kayleigh McEnany, citing "a mountain of evidence" for conviction.
story: Attorney Edward Paltzik tells Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany that Lindsay Clancy holdout juror Michael Desronvil had "zero doubt" and "a mountain of evidence" behind his decision.

The attorney for the lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial is pushing back on a claim that his client refused to follow the law, telling Fox News host Kayleigh McEnany that the juror had no doubt about his decision.

In a preview of an interview airing Monday on "Fox & Friends," McEnany asked attorney Edward Paltzik whether juror Michael P. Desronvil ever had reasonable doubt after the jury foreperson sent the judge a note accusing him of refusing to follow the law on reasonable doubt.
"Michael had zero doubt," Paltzik said.
LINDSAY CLANCY ATTORNEY KEVIN REDDINGTON FIRES BACK AT LONE HOLDOUT JUROR'S ATTORNEY AFTER FIERY INTERVIEW
Attorney Edward Paltzik represents Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial. (Fox News)
"Zero doubt. No doubt, and he had evidence to back up his position?" McEnany responded.
"A lot of evidence, a mountain of evidence," Paltzik said.
LINDSAY CLANCY JUROR ADMITTED 'REASONABLE DOUBT' BUT STILL REFUSED INSANITY VERDICT, FOREPERSON SAYS
Michael P. Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. (Fugitive TV)

Desronvil was the lone holdout after seven days of deliberations in Clancy’s trial. Eleven jurors were prepared to find the former labor and delivery nurse not criminally responsible for killing her three children, while Desronvil held out for a conviction. Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial Sept. 4.

Clancy admitted killing 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson and 8-month-old Callan at the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in January 2023. Her defense argued that postpartum psychosis left her not criminally responsible. Prosecutors argued she understood what she was doing and planned the killings.
LINDSAY CLANCY DA RARELY DOES PLEA DEALS, BUT HER CASE COULD BE THE 'EXCEPTION,' VETERAN ATTORNEY SAYS
Lindsay Clancy in court last month. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Desronvil later said he believed the physical evidence and witness testimony showed Clancy knew what she was doing. Prosecutors have not announced whether they will retry her. She is due back in court Sept. 29.

Fox News reached out to defense attorney Kevin Reddington to get a response to the accusations, and he has chosen not to reply to our inquiries.
Watch McEnany’s full interview with Paltzik Monday on "Fox & Friends."

title: Police hunt sexually violent predator who vanished after GPS 'tamper mode' alert
summary: Merle Wakefield had been on conditional release since November 2024 with GPS monitoring. Now, the convicted sex offender is missing in San Diego County.
story: Chicago faces a crisis as hundreds of alleged criminals, released on electronic ankle monitors, are now missing. Mike Tobin reports on the Cook County pre-trial program where 246 participants are AWOL, including individuals charged with murder, sexual assault and aggravated battery. Former police chief Tom Weitzel criticizes the system's significant security gaps.
A convicted child sex offender was still missing Sunday, two days after his GPS monitor sounded a tamper alert at a San Diego worksite and supervisors arrived to find him gone, authorities said.
Merle Wakefield, 69, was working in Rancho Bernardo when his device alerted to "Tamper Mode" at about 3:30 a.m. Friday, according to the San Diego County Sheriff’s Office.
Liberty Healthcare, the state contractor supervising him, responded to the location and found the device removed and Wakefield gone. The company notified the sheriff’s office and San Diego police.
ACCUSED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT MURDERER WHO FLED US DURING 48-HOUR PASS HAD ACCESS TO TAXPAYER-FUNDED APARTMENT
The most recent mugshot of Merle Wakefield, who is wanted after disappearing in San Diego County. (San Diego County Sheriff's Office)
The sheriff’s office said Sunday it "shares the community’s concerns over Merle Wakefield’s disappearance" and was still actively looking for him.
"We have been working diligently to locate him," the agency said. It asked the public to report any sightings or information that could help find Wakefield.
CALIFORNIA DEMS TRIGGER OUTRAGE AFTER SIDING WITH CONVICTED CHILD SEX OFFENDERS IN SHOCKING VOTE

"It’s been more than 48 hours since Merle Wakefield took off his GPS monitor and walked away. He’s still out there," San Diego County Supervisor Jim Desmond wrote Sunday on Facebook. He called Wakefield "a convicted child molester and violent rapist" and accused the state of saying nothing publicly about his disappearance.

Wakefield is wanted for violating the terms of his conditional release, the sheriff’s office said. He was convicted in 1980 and 1991 of lewd or lascivious acts with a child under 14 and rape by force, according to the agency. He has been on conditional release since November 2024.
MACHETE-WIELDING MS-13 GANGSTER WANTED FOR MURDER WALKS FREE AFTER BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE RELEASES HIM: DHS
A 2024 mugshot of Merle Wakefield, who has been on conditional release since November of that year. (San Diego County Sheriff's Office)
Desmond said Wakefield was gone by the time Liberty Healthcare arrived after the GPS alert.

"That’s how easy it was," he wrote in an earlier post. "The state released him into our community in November 2024 and promised he’d be monitored and supervised. Less than two years later, he’s missing and wanted."
DHS UNLOADS ON 'SANCTUARY CALAMITY' VIRGINIA AFTER ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF HEINOUS CRIME RELEASED: 'SICKO'

Local officials had warned about Wakefield’s release before it happened. A San Diego judge granted him a transient release in October 2024 rather than placing him in a designated home, Fox 5/KUSI reported at the time. It was the third attempt to place him in San Diego County.

An earlier proposal would have placed Wakefield in a Poway home near a school and park, prompting residents to rally against it, according to the outlet. Poway Mayor Steve Vaus opposed that location and argued that allowing Wakefield to live without a fixed address would make it harder for the public to know where he was.
BIDEN ADMIN'S 'PREDATOR' RELEASE PUTS VIRGINIA'S SANCTUARY POLICIES BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT
A 2021 mugshot of Merle Wakefield, who is wanted for violating the terms of his conditional release. (San Diego County District Attorney's Office)
"It’s a shell game that puts a community at risk," Vaus told Fox 5/KUSI about the transient release.

The San Diego County District Attorney’s Office also opposed releasing Wakefield without a fixed residence, citing concerns about limited monitoring and supervision. Spokesperson Tanya Sierra told the outlet that the Department of State Hospitals and Liberty Healthcare needed to find suitable housing where people granted conditional release could be closely monitored.
SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: SOFT-ON-CRIME JUDGES NEED CONSEQUENCES. THE JAIL ACT DELIVERS
California Senate Minority Leader Brian W. Jones, R-San Diego, is shown. (Reuters/Reuters Photos)
State Sen. Brian Jones raised his own concerns about where Wakefield would stay. He told Fox 5/KUSI that Wakefield might end up on the streets or in a hotel at taxpayer expense.
"Supposedly, he’s going to have a tracking device," Jones said at the time.
NEW YORK BILLS COULD ABOLISH LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE FOR SERIAL KILLERS AND COP KILLERS, CRITICS WARN

Jones had also called for an audit of California’s sexually violent predator program, the outlet reported. The audit found that about 36% of participants had violated the terms of their release. Jones criticized the program’s cost and argued that the state should keep sexually violent predators in hospitals rather than place them in communities.

The California Department of State Hospitals pushed back on criticism of the release process, telling Fox 5/KUSI that the court ultimately decides whether someone designated a sexually violent predator can be conditionally released.
SEXUAL PREDATOR ‘COOKIE MONSTER’ CAUGHT IN TERRIFIED CHILD’S BED DURING MIDNIGHT BREAK-IN, POLICE SAY

The department said its supervision program used GPS monitoring, unannounced home visits and surveillance, and that breaking the rules could send someone back to a state hospital. The outlet also reported that Wakefield’s court order called for 24-hour in-person supervision wherever he stayed. That report was published before the hearing to finalize his release.
Desmond renewed his objection after Wakefield disappeared.

"I’ve fought these placements from day one," he wrote. "These people do not belong back out in the community. They belong in a state hospital or in jail. As long as Sacramento’s law keeps putting them in our neighborhoods, families are going to keep paying the price."

Wakefield is 5 feet, 10 inches tall, weighs 230 pounds and has brown eyes, according to the sheriff’s office. Authorities warned anyone who sees him not to approach or contact him and to call 911 or local law enforcement.

title: Texas clinic owner convicted in $26M military health fraud tied to gold-plated Cybertruck
summary: Kevin D. Curry used TRICARE kickbacks to fund a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck and lavish parties after billing $26 million in fake TMS therapy claims.
story: Medicaid fraud allegations target applied behavioral analysis therapy services for children with autism, raising concerns among families. Christina Coleman reports on the rise in fraudulent billing practices as mother Lindsey Chaney and Kelsey Bennett from the Autism Families Alliance join the discussion to highlight the impact of these fraudulent schemes.

A Texas mental health clinic owner was convicted by a federal jury after prosecutors said he orchestrated a $26 million scheme to defraud the military's health care program, using some of the proceeds to fund luxury purchases, including a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck worth more than $100,000.

Kevin D. Curry, 64, of Frisco, was found guilty Thursday in federal court in Fort Worth on three counts of health care fraud, three counts of offering and paying illegal health care kickbacks and three counts of engaging in monetary transactions in criminally derived property, according to the Justice Department.

Federal prosecutors said Curry exploited TRICARE, the health care program serving active-duty servicemembers, retirees and their families, by billing for transcranial magnetic stimulation, or TMS, therapy that was medically unnecessary or, in many cases, never provided.
FBI LAUNCHES 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST AS DOJ CHARGES OHIO DEFENDANTS IN $30M MEDICAID SCHEME FOR KIDS
A gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck that federal prosecutors said Kevin Curry purchased with proceeds from a $26 million scheme to defraud TRICARE. (DOJ)

According to evidence presented at trial, Curry owned and operated mental health clinics in Plano and Fort Worth, Texas, as well as Fort Walton Beach, Florida. Prosecutors said he paid more than $5.5 million in illegal kickbacks to persuade active-duty servicemembers, veterans and their family members to consent to TMS therapy they did not qualify for and, in many instances, did not receive.

Judge Leonie Brinkema said the issues underlying a lawsuit over the Anti-Weaponization Fund remain "alive and kicking," despite the Justice Department’s insistence that the fund is dead. (Photo by Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

The Justice Department said Curry falsely represented himself as a medical doctor, used licensed doctors' credentials without their knowledge or consent to submit claims to TRICARE, and directed employees to fabricate medical records to justify fraudulent billings.
FRAUD EXPERT EXPOSES HOW HIDDEN NETWORKS DROVE MINNESOTA FRAUD, OTHER MAJOR SCAMS: 'CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE'
Authorities said Curry's clinics submitted more than $26 million in false, fraudulent or kickback-tainted claims to TRICARE, which ultimately paid approximately $17 million.

Justice Department lawyers asked a federal judge Friday to dismiss a lawsuit challenging the Anti-Weaponization Fund, arguing Attorney General Todd Blanche formally terminated it Aug. 2. (Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
Prosecutors said Curry laundered some of the proceeds by spending the money on luxury hotel stays, a lavish casino-themed party and a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck valued at more than $100,000.
TAXPAYER FUNDS MEANT FOR LA HOMELESS ALLEGEDLY SPENT ON TAHITI TRIP, NIGHTCLUB, LUXURY CARS: FEDS

"This defendant exploited a critical health care program serving active-duty servicemembers and their families, diverting taxpayer dollars to bankroll personal luxuries ranging from hotel stays to a casino-themed party and even a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald said in a statement.

U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould said Curry "shamelessly preyed on the trust of servicemembers, veterans, and their families," accusing him of fabricating medical records, stealing doctors' identities and submitting fraudulent claims while profiting from kickback-tainted money.

title: Florida sex offender accused of babysitting ad trap as police investigate potential interstate predator

story: Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill and Livingston Parish Sheriff Jason Ard are leading the fight against child predators online, as they warn children are being lured over gaming apps and social media.

Georgia investigators are searching for potential victims of a convicted Florida sex offender after DNA linked him to three sexual assault cases involving women allegedly lured through Craigslist job ads.

Julius Hunter, 42, faces rape, aggravated sodomy and kidnapping charges in Georgia in connection with a 2016 attack on a 19-year-old teen at a Clarkston apartment complex. A DeKalb County grand jury indicted him on Aug. 11.

Before his Georgia arrest, Hunter pleaded no contest in an unrelated 2021 Florida sexual battery case involving his former girlfriend. Investigators are now examining what they believe is a broader pattern of sexual assaults.

Julius Hunter, center, was arrested in Fort Lauderdale, right, in connection with a sexual assault in Clarkston, Georgia, left. (DeKalb County Sheriff's Office; Joe Raedle/Getty Images; REUTERS/Carlos Barria)
FIANCÉE STICKS BY ACCUSED SERIAL RAPIST AS SPECIAL AGENTS DEFEND TAILING HIM FOR RESTAURANT DNA STAKEOUT
"Hunter grew up in New Jersey, so it is possible there may be victims there," DeKalb County District Attorney Investigator Brandi Rogers told Fox News Digital.
Hunter's DNA also matched evidence from two additional sexual assault cases in DeKalb and Gwinnett counties in 2016 and 2017, authorities said.
REPEAT OFFENDER WITH 7 PRIOR CONVICTIONS ARRESTED 3 TIMES IN 12 DAYS OVER ALLEGED ATTACKS ON WOMEN
He has not been charged in either case. Rogers said investigators have been unable to reconnect with the two women.
$300 babysitting job

The 19-year-old thought she was heading to a $300 overnight babysitting job when Hunter arranged a ride-share to an apartment near 700 Jolly Avenue on July 27, 2016, according to the DeKalb County District Attorney’s Office.
When she arrived, there were no children — only Hunter and another man, authorities said.
Julius Hunter was charged in a sexual assault case in Clarkston, Georgia. (Gregory Rec/Portland Press Herald via Getty Images)

DNA TECHNOLOGY LEADS TO ARREST IN 1988 KILLING OF ORLANDO WOMAN AFTER NEARLY FOUR DECADES

Florida arrest leads to DNA match

The Clarkston case remained unsolved for years after the Georgia Bureau of Investigation developed a male DNA profile from the 19-year-old’s sexual assault kit. The profile was entered into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) but, at the time, did not match anyone in the national database.

title: Motorcycle patrols swarm Iranian cities, checkpoints rise as regime braces for unrest
summary: Sources told Fox News Digital that IRGC, Basij and police have flooded Tehran with checkpoints and patrols as student protests over compulsory hijab grow.
story: Images from Tehran show Iranian women openly defying mandatory hijab rules, confronting the regime's oppressive rules.

Iranian security forces have stepped up their presence in Tehran and other cities, with motorcycle patrols, checkpoints and forces positioned across major urban areas as authorities brace for possible unrest, multiple sources inside Iran told Fox News Digital.

The security buildup comes as university students have returned to the streets in Tehran, protesting compulsory hijab rules, rising education costs and political repression, videos published on Iran International show.

Sources inside Iran confirmed to Fox News Digital that motorcycle units have been operating across Tehran and other cities during events surrounding Iran’s annual "Sacred Defense Week," while members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Basij and law enforcement have been positioned at major squares and other locations.
IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS
Motorcyclists ride during a state-organized motorcycle parade called "Janfada," meaning "Sacrifice for Iran," in Tehran, Iran, Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. (Vahid Salemi/AP Photo)
The sources also said security personnel have stopped pedestrians, searched some individuals and examined mobile phones, including material authorities consider "anti-regime."

The accounts follow a report from the National Council of Resistance of Iran’s (NCRI's) Committee on Security and Counterterrorism alleging that Iranian authorities ordered a "100%" state of readiness for the Army, IRGC, Basij and law enforcement and canceled leave through Sept. 27. The NCRI also claimed 51,000 personnel had been deployed across Greater Tehran, including 30,000 IRGC and Basij members and 21,000 law enforcement personnel. The reported preparations are taking place as signs of public unrest have begun resurfacing on university campuses. Fox News Digital has not independently confirmed those claims.
One source in Tehran told Fox News Digital that the heightened security presence extends beyond what is visible on the streets.
INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE'
Motorcyclists ride during a state-organized motorcycle parade called "Janfada," meaning "Sacrifice for Iran,"in Tehran, Iran, Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. (Vahid Salemi/AP)
"Motorcyclists taking photos of shops, and prisoners being threatened and forced to tell their families not to physically participate in any protests that might arise," the source said.

The source said Basij members who previously received military training have been placed on alert and are being housed or assembled at educational facilities and large properties on the outskirts of Tehran.

The measures were not limited to the capital. "This situation exists in all cities, but the nature of the presence and the way things are organized differ," the source told Fox News Digital, citing information received from Borujen, Isfahan and other cities.
IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP
Military members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in western Tehran, Iran. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"In those places, plainclothes agents are more prevalent and try to remain out of public view; however, in Tehran, they appear openly on the streets in military uniforms and gear specifically to instill fear and terror," the source said, adding that leave had also been canceled in smaller cities and claimed shops, telephone communications and everyday activities were under increased surveillance.
Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi, who lives outside Iran after years of opposition activity, separately told Fox News Digital that he had received similar accounts.

"I’ve received reports of new checkpoints being set up in Tehran, and there have also been reports of military forces being put on alert, as well as civilians who had previously been trained by the regime for urban repression being called up," Ghadimi added that people are being detained on espionage charges simply because they communicate with people outside of Iran.
IRAN INMATES SEW LIPS SHUT IN MASS HUNGER STRIKE AT NOTORIOUS US-SANCTIONED JAIL: REPORT
Members of the Basij paramilitary force stand at a checkpoint in Tehran, Iran, Sunday, March 29, 2026. (Vahid Salemi/AP Photo)

Ghadimi also said he had received reports that individuals with serious criminal records had been released from prison in exchange for reporting to local Basij bases and participating in the suppression of demonstrations.

Students at Allameh Tabataba’i University in Tehran held a protest Monday against compulsory hijab, rising tuition and university living conditions, according to videos reported by Iran International on Sept. 28 and 29. Students were recorded chanting against the morality police and political repression.

Iran International reported that the protest began over tuition, dormitory and food costs before expanding into broader political chants. The outlet, citing the student publication Amirkabir, reported that Basij members attempted to disrupt the gathering and threatened students.
IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS. THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN

The protests also come amid renewed pressure over compulsory hijab rules on university campuses. On Sept. 8, Iran International reported that a senior official in the office representing Iran’s supreme leader at universities said a new compulsory-hijab directive for universities had been drafted and was expected to be issued by the ministries overseeing higher education.

Separately, the IRGC escalated its rhetoric toward Washington on Tuesday, with spokesman Hossein Mohebbi calling on Americans to pressure President Donald Trump’s administration. "This lying administration must be changed," Mohebbi said at a Tehran press conference, according to Reuters video distributed Sept. 29.
His remarks came as U.S. and Iranian officials continued indirect contacts through mediators in an effort to end the seven-month conflict, Reuters reported.
The combination of visible security preparations and renewed demonstrations is fueling speculation among Iranians about whether the country could face another broader wave of unrest.

Members of the Iranian police stand guard at a protest in front of the British embassy following anti-government protests in Tehran, Iran, January 14, 2026. (Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via)
"The reality is that nobody knows what’s going to happen," Ghadimi told Fox News Digital. "Everyone I talk to says that this situation cannot continue and that, somehow, it has to come to an end."

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition.
