title: Ahead of rare execution, lone woman on Tennessee’s death row says ‘I am at peace’
summary: Christa Pike, 50, was an accomplice in a murder she committed at 18. She would be the first woman executed by the state in over 200 years.
story: With her execution days away, the lone woman on Tennessee’s death row says she is prepared to die but “nervous” about how the state intends to carry it out.

Before learning Monday that Gov. Bill Lee would not be intervening in her case, Christa Pike wrote in a letter to NBC News, shared by her spiritual adviser: “Whether my clemency is granted or not, I am at peace.”
“I am not afraid to die,” wrote Pike, who has been on death row for over three decades. “I’m only nervous about the process.”
Tennessee is poised to execute Pike, 50, on Wednesday by lethal injection — the first time in more than 200 years that the state will put a woman to death, according to historical records.

In 1995, Pike was 18 when Knoxville police say she and two teenage accomplices worked together to torture, slash and fatally beat Colleen Slemmer, 19. Police say Pike and the others lured Slemmer, a classmate in their Job Corps training program, to an abandoned steam plant at the nearby University of Tennessee and attacked her.

The case became sensationalized when investigators said it was tied to the occult because someone had carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest and Pike bragged to another student that she had kept a fragment of the victim’s skull as a “souvenir.”

title: New York Times executive fatally shot by his in-laws in Bay Area park, police say
summary: Jonathan McKinsey, head of engineering and games player experiences for the Times, was found on the ground at a park with multiple gunshot wounds, police said.
story: A New York Times engineering executive was killed by his in-laws Saturday amid an ongoing domestic and child abuse legal battle, according to Bay Area police.

The shooting unfolded Saturday afternoon in the city of Dublin in Alameda County shortly after 3 p.m. A Dublin police officer found Jonathan McKinsey, head of engineering and games player experiences for the Times, lying on the ground at Dublin Sports Grounds with multiple gunshot wounds, police said.
He was pronounced dead at the scene.
After receiving a flood of witness phone calls, Dublin police found and arrested two suspects: Shouyong Zhang, 77, and Shili Chen, 77, a married couple who were identified as McKinsey’s in-laws.
They are both being held at the Santa Rita Jail pending charges, police said in a statement.

According to court documents, McKinsey and his wife, Candice Jang, were embroiled in a child custody battle when he died. Last year, a judge granted Jang’s petition for a domestic violence temporary restraining order against McKinsey, court documents show. McKinsey filed for divorce in December, and a hearing was scheduled for next month.
In August, the court approved hiring a private child custody evaluator.

McKinsey, 40, earned a bachelor’s degree from Georgia Tech before receiving his master’s in computer science at the University of California, Berkeley. He had worked at the Times since 2023, the Times confirmed.

title: University of Georgia student dancing on couch near window falls 8 stories and survives
summary: A University of Georgia student survived a plunge from her eighth-floor apartment, authorities said Monday, after she had been “dancing on a couch near a window” and fell out.
story: A University of Georgia student survived a plunge from her eighth-floor apartment, authorities said Monday, after she had been “dancing on a couch near a window” and fell out.
The terrifying fall from the Rambler Athens Apartments at 558 W. Broad St. in Athens happened at about 7:30 p.m. Saturday, according to police records.

The “student was dancing on a couch near a window that was open” and “fell from the 8th floor window and landed on the pool deck below,” the Athens-Clarke County Police Department said in a statement to NBC News.
Remarkably, 21-year-old Virginia native Kristen Elizabeth Sargent appeared to have survived this harrowing plunge.
“At this time, she is conscious and alert but seriously injured,” police added.
A cushioned metal bench might have broken the 5-foot-7, 115-pound woman’s fall.

“I arrived and spoke with bystanders who advised that the female victim had been dancing on a couch or air mattress which was near an open window and had apparently fallen through the screen and onto the ground below,” according to a report by ACC police Sgt. Erik Ellison.

“When I arrived, the victim was on the ground near the pool, which at this complex is in a courtyard on the second floor of the building. It appeared from the scene that the victim had struck a metal bench as she fell, as the cushion on the bench had some blood on it and the armrest of the bench had broken off.”
The initial probe “thus far suggests that this was an accident” and that the victim “will survive,” Ellison added.

title: In reversal, Justice Samuel Alito steps aside from major climate case
summary: Alito will sit out the first case the Supreme Court hears this term after facing calls from the left to do so because he owns stock in oil companies. He had previously pushed back.
story: WASHINGTON — Conservative Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito will no longer participate in a major climate change case after facing calls that he recuse himself because of his stock holdings in oil companies.
The new development was disclosed in a letter dated Monday and sent to lawyers involved in the case, with no reason given.
“Justice Alito has determined that he will not continue to participate in this case,” the letter said.
Add to Google
Add to Google

Alito had, via a court spokeswoman, previously told NBC News there was no need for him to step aside from the case, which is being argued next week and could have broad nationwide implications when the court issues a ruling.

Left-leaning groups have repeatedly called for Alito’s recusal from the case, in which ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy are seeking to toss out a Colorado lawsuit seeking damages from the oil companies for the impacts of climate change.

Although Alito does not own stocks in either company, he does hold stocks in oil companies ConocoPhillips and Phillips 66, as well as five other firms involved in the energy sector, his financial disclosure report says.

Activists calling for his recusal said the companies he holds stocks in could benefit if the Supreme Court throws out the Colorado case, brought by the city and county of Boulder, because it could directly affect similar cases across the country in which they are among the defendants.
The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. With Alito stepping aside, it raises the possibility of a 4-4 split, which would leave the major legal issues unresolved.

The oil and gas industry is hoping the court will issue a broad ruling that would prevent cases like the one in Colorado from moving forward in state courts, potentially saving it from paying out billions of dollars in damages.
Earlier in the litigation, in 2023, Alito did recuse himself when the court turned away an appeal from the companies in the Colorado case.
On the same day, the court rejected appeals in similar cases involving other companies, including ConocoPhillips and Phillips 66. Alito also did not participate in those cases.
In May, a court spokesman said Alito had “inadvertently recused” in the earlier Colorado case.

“Justice Alito does not have a financial interest in any party” involved in the case, the court spokeswoman said in a statement provided to NBC News at the time. Alito was advised by the court’s legal counsel that “his recusal is not required,” she added.
That was before the most recent calls for Alito to step aside based on the indirect benefit he could obtain from a ruling in favor of Exxon and Suncor.

Earlier this month, an advocacy group called Consumer Watchdog pointed to disclosures made by ConocoPhillips and Phillips 66 to shareholders in which they warned of the risks the companies face as a result of climate lawsuits making similar claims to the Colorado case.
“Justice Alito’s recusal ... is the right decision, and one he should have made from the start,” Alexandra Nagy, the group’s organizing director, said in a statement.
The Supreme Court spokeswoman did not immediately respond to a request seeking further comment.

Some conservatives have also pushed for liberal Justice Elena Kagan to recuse herself in the case because of a controversy over a chapter on climate change included in, and subsequently removed from, a reference manual for judges. Kagan wrote a brief foreword to the manual and recently told lawmakers that she never read the chapter in question.

title: Trump unveils plans for a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa
summary: Mesabi Metallics, which is building the plant, aims to start production in 2030, a White House official said.
story: President Donald Trump on Monday announced a plan for a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa.

“This steel will be mined, melted and made right here in the USA, which is something very unusual,” Trump said in the Oval Office, where he was joined by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; Joe Broking, the CEO of the company building the plant; and other business leaders.

Mesabi Metallics is constructing the plant with the aim of starting production by 2030, a White House official said. The facility is expected to produce 10 million tons of steel a year and create as many as 1,750 permanent jobs in the state, the official said.
The plant will be capable of supporting defense sector requirements for high-grade steel, the official said.
The president said the plant will “produce some of the highest quality, most affordable steel anywhere in the world.”
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on the new facility.

The announcement comes weeks ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with Iowa in the center of the fight for the Senate and the House. Democrats are also challenging for the governorship after 16 years of uninterrupted Republican control of the state’s top office.

The plant will use iron ore from a new mine that the company invested $2.5 billion to build in Minnesota. The mine, which will come online in the coming weeks, will produce about 7.5 million tons of iron per year and create about 350 jobs in the state, the White House official said.

The mine is based in Minnesota’s Mesabi Iron Range, which stretches 80 to 100 miles and contributed about 60% of total iron ore production in the U.S. during the 20th century, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.
“It’s the first new iron ore mine in the United States in more than 50 years,” Trump said.
The Export-Import Bank, the federal government’s export credit agency, will issue up to $10 billion in financing for Mesabi Metallics’ expansion there, an agency release said.

Trump has prioritized expanding the U.S. manufacturing sector, including by taking aim at steel imports as part of a wide-ranging trade policy. Although the Supreme Court this year struck down many of the tariffs he imposed, it did leave duties in place on imported steel and aluminum. The U.S. levies a 50% tariff on most steel imports.
Trump on Monday touted his efforts to try to reinvigorate the industry.

“Soon after my inauguration, I imposed powerful 50% tariffs on all foreign steel, and now our steel industry is roaring back to life,” he said. “Everyone’s building their plant here because they don’t want to pay tariffs.”
In a letter last week, steel industry groups urged Trump to “stand firm against efforts to weaken the tariffs” as U.S. steelmakers invest in new mills domestically.
“Weakening the tariffs now would put that progress at risk, threatening American jobs and the economic and national security benefits the policy was designed to protect,” they warned.

title: Dylan Sprouse Reveals ‘Lovely’ Name of 1st Child with Barbara Palvin
summary: Dylan Sprouse and Barbara Palvin have welcomed their first child!
story: Dylan Sprouse and Barbara Palvin have welcomed their first child!
The former “Suite Life of Zack and Cody” star, 33, and his model wife, 32, announced on Instagram on Sept. 28 that Palvin has given birth to a baby girl.

The diehard Los Angeles Dodgers fans shared a photo holding their baby girl dressed in a Dodgers onesie while watching the team play. Palvin is decked out in a Shohei Ohtani jersey, and Sprouse wears a Miguel Rojas jersey.
“We took Labor Day literally this year,” Palvin captioned the photo.
Palvin confirmed they welcomed a daughter by posting a photo to her Instagram story of Sprouse holding the infant close and captioning it, “Daddy’s girl already.”
Sprouse also revealed his daughter’s name on the Sept. 29 episode of his “Wildmen” podcast: Sylvie.
“She’s very lovely. Her name is Sylvie,” Sprouse said. “Sylvie Sprouse. She’s a very well behaved baby.”

The little girl will watch her first Dodgers playoff games this year when the two-time defending World Series champions play the winner of this week’s Braves-Phillies series in the National League Division Series, which begins on Oct. 3 at Dodger Stadium.

In May, Sprouse and Palvin announced on Instagram that they were expecting their first child. Their joint post featured a sonogram image of a baby’s hand making a “rock on” symbol. A second image showed Sprouse and Palvin’s hands making the same gesture.
The couple’s announcement came the same day Palvin showed off a baby bump alongside Sprouse at the Cannes Film Festival in France.
The two have been married since July 2023. They got engaged in September 2022 after five years of dating.

title: The Best Principal Ever? Mr. Belding Was the Guiding Voice on ‘Saved by the Bell’
summary: Mr. Belding, the principal on “Saved by the Bell” played by Dennis Haskins, has died. Here’s a look back on his legacy
story: If you’re in your 40s or 50s, there’s a good chance you woke up this morning to a flurry of text messages from friends sharing a link that “Saved by the Bell” star Dennis Haskins had died.

Haskins, who died at the age of 75, played Mr. Belding, the principal of fictional Bayside High School on the long-running 1990s Saturday morning franchise. He cared deeply about his students, while playing the foil to the scheming Zack Morris, played by Mark-Paul Gosselaar.

Armed with a catch phrase — “Hey, hey, hey, what is going on here?” — the perpetually cheery and often exasperated Mr. Belding was somewhat frazzled and a step behind Zack and the Bayside crew, but he always caught on and always led them on the straight and narrow. He was funny, but he was caring, the kind of adult kids enjoyed watching on Saturday mornings.

There’s a place for Mr. Belding on the Mount Rushmore of fictional principals. Haskins’ combination of comic timing, compassion and chemistry with the cast congealed to make Mr. Belding a beloved character, complete with a silly name that elicited images of a goofball that belied his intelligence.
“A cranky editor from Universal,” “Saved by the Bell” producer Peter Engel told TODAY.com in 2019 about who the inspiration for the name was.

Whether he was getting duped into improperly trimming a bonsai tree by Screech so Zack could try and win a free trip to Hawaii, freaking out when his wife went into labor after an earthquake or lending advice after Slater mourned the death of his pet chameleon, Mr. Belding was a rock, the kind of principal who may seem somewhat clueless and goofy on the surface, but underneath was a pillar of strength and wisdom for his students.

Haskins portrayed Mr. Belding in “Good Morning, Miss Bliss,” the original iteration of “Saved by the Bell,” and would go on to play him for all four years that “Saved by the Bell” aired on NBC. He also played him in the TV movies “Saved by the Bell: Hawaiian Style” and “Saved by the Bell: Wedding in Las Vegas.”

In addition, he played the character on an episode of “Saved by the Bell: The College Years,” and would portray him for another 143 episodes on “Saved by the Bell: The New Class” over the course of its entire seven-season run. It’s rare for one actor to be so associated with one character for so long.

Haskins is the second “Saved by the Bell” cast member to die, following Dustin Diamond, who died in 2021. Diamond, who played Screech, endured a complicated life after his time playing the character came to an end, but Haskins’ legacy isn’t as sad.

“Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more,” his agent, Jay Schachter, said in a statement following his death. “He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans.”
His fans also loved him. Haskins made personal appearances at everything from minor league baseball games to college campuses over the years.

If you know “Saved by the Bell,” you can conjure images of Mr. Belding going toe to toe with Zack while trying to teach him right from wrong, the threat of detention hanging overhead like the threat of a Valley prank. Zack’s capers were often thwarted by Mr. Belding, but, in the end, Zack did learn and come to appreciate his principal.

“You know, son, you’ve got something very special inside of you. I hope I’m around to see it when you let it all out,” Mr. Belding tells Zack in the graduation episode before they share a hug, representing a moment where Zack truly understands just how much Mr. Belding meant to him.
Haskins isn’t around to see the outpouring of love his fans still have for him. But, have no doubt, they do.

title: Netflix’s Hockey Romance ‘Icebreaker’ Casts its 2 Leads
summary: Netflix has announced the two leads taking center of the ice in their upcoming series “Icebreaker,” based off the bestselling novel by Hannah Grace.
story: Netflix has announced the two leads taking center of the ice in their upcoming series “Icebreaker,” based off the bestselling novel by Hannah Grace.
Daisy Jelley and Connor Simos have been announced to play the series’ leading couple, Anastasia “Stassie” Allen and Nate Hawkins, for the book’s adaptation.

Anastasia Allen is a competitive figure skater with her eyes on the Olympic prize. Nate Hawkins is the equally competitive captain of the hockey team. When the two are forced to share their campus’ single ice rink for practices, things begin to heat up as the pair are forced to work together to reach their individual goals.

Grace’s “Icebreaker” was first conceived as a viral Wattpad series before being published as a novel and spending 70 consecutive weeks on the New York Times bestseller list following its release. In June, Netflix announced that it would be bringing the book to life at the BANFF World Media Festival.
The novel was also a big hit on BookTok, TikTok’s avid reading community, where fans have posted raving book reviews and potential “fan-casts” in anticipation for the TV series.

Netflix has not yet announced the show’s official release date. But with Jelley and Simos stepping into the story’s framing roles, fans should be on the look out for future cast announcements and trailers.
Here’s a closer look at our two unlikely ice-mates.
Daisy Jelley as Anastasia

Jelley will be stepping into the role of Anastasia “Stassie” Allen, a strong-willed competitive figure skater and the novel’s female protagonist. Viewers may recognize the 26-year-old English actress from her roles in “How to Have Sex” as Gemma and “Geek Girl” as Poppy.
Connor Simos as Nate
Simos will be playing Jelley’s icy counterpart and eventual love interest Nate Hawkins, the good-natured captain of the Maple Hills hockey team.
Simos is in the upcoming Chris Hemsworth thriller “Subversion.” This is his first TV role.

title: Jasmine Guy Shuts Down Criticism of Her Appearance Amid Revival of ‘A Different World’
summary: Jasmine Guy is calling out critics who have been posting negative comments about her appearance following the release of the “A Different World” revival.
story: Jasmine Guy is calling out critics who have been posting negative comments about her appearance following the release of the “A Different World” revival.

On Sept. 24, fans of the beloved sitcom were reunited with Guy and her character Whitley when the actor reprised her role in the series’ Netflix reboot. Guy was joined by Kadeem Hardison, Darryl M. Bell and Cree Summers, who all had special guest appearances in the new show.
But while many fans were happy to see Whitley, Dwayne, Ron and Freddie together again, others began comparing Guy to the ‘80s version of herself.
She reacted to the comments in an Instagram post Sept. 27.
“The internet can be brutal to women as we grow older. It asks us to celebrate life while criticizing every sign that we’ve lived it,” she said.
Guy continued, “Growing older brings change, and I won’t pretend every change is easy. But beauty, style, and joy don’t have an expiration date.”

She encouraged followers to not spend their time judging themselves or each other and instead focus on loving one another “making memories, and living the life we’re here to live.” She also added Al Green’s “Simply Beautiful” to the post.
Celebrity friends and fans applauded her uplifting message and left supportive replies.
Tina Knowles praised Guy for being an “Accomplished , Beautiful, graceful, Lady.”
Tatyana Ali called the 64-year-old actor “gorgeous” and included multiple crowns, sparkle and a red rose emoji.
Co-star Cornell Young IV, who plays Shaquille Johnson in the revival, commented, “You are so Gorgeous! Even a more Gorgeous soul! I love you.”

One fan chimed in, “You are THEEEE JASMINE GUY. An icon, then and now. The internet can be so cruel to women for simply living long enough to age, but please know so many of us see your beauty, your talent, and the legacy you’ve built. We love you!”

Despite some negative posts, Guy has been busy celebrating the return of “A Different World” on social media, sharing praise from fans about the original and the revival on her Instagram stories. Fans have also been uploading scenes from their favorite episodes of the sitcom, which ran from 1987 to 1993 for six seasons.
Guy, Summers and Bell stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Sept. 23 to chat about the Netflix show and share some behind-the-scenes stories from their time filming the original.
Guy revealed that although Whitley and Dwayne were the couple viewers rooted for, in real life Hardison was dating Summer.
“I do really love him, but he was seeing her,” Guy said about Hardison as she pointed to Summer.
She quipped that the set was “quite incestuous.”
Guy then confirmed that she dated Dominic Hoffman, who played one of Whitley’s love interests, when the show aired.
“It sounds very ‘Brady Bunch’-y,” she joked.

title: The Best Dressed Stars of the 2026 VMAs, According to 3 Fashion Experts
summary: Who are the best dressed stars from the VMAs 2026 red carpet? We asked three fashion experts
story: If there’s one red carpet where fashion rules are meant to be broken, it’s the MTV VMAs.

This year, stars leaned all the way in, serving up sheer fabrics, lace, corsets, rhinestones, dramatic silhouettes and plenty of skin. Also at the 2026 awards ceremony, Taylor Swift arrived in a “Patient Zero”-inspired dress, Adam Lambert wore a headpiece spelling out his name, Brandon Sklenar went blond and Sombr had an unforgettable belt.
Fashion experts Maggie Gillette, a principal at The Curio, Julie DuRocher, design director at Jovani, and bridal fashion designer Hayley Paige weigh in on the night’s standout style moments.
Paris Hilton
DuRocher is loving Paris Hilton’s fresh take on red carpet glamour.

“Paris Hilton is giving us a very new-age look,” DuRocher says. “I love how polished and modern it feels while still having that signature Paris glamour. It feels fresh for her and perfectly suited to the VMAs.”
Lucky Daye
The R&B singer’s Campillo ensemble was Gillette’s standout among the men’s fashion.
“The wrap detail felt so chic and I love that they used a clasp instead of buttons as a closure,” Gillette says, particularly praising the unusual fastening.
To Gillette, the detail feels like a natural progression of another menswear trend. “It felt like the evolution to the men’s brooch trend we’ve been seeing on celebs this year.”
She also loved the fabric’s subtle sheen, noting that “that’s atypical for menswear and works so well here!”
Normani
Normani’s ensemble struck DuRocher as a cool mix of sexy, feminine and fashion forward.

“I love the combination of that jersey-like, leather-inspired look with the dramatic flower at the dropped torso and the fit-and-flare silhouette,” she says. “It feels cool and fashion-forward while still being very feminine.”
For DuRocher, the overall effect is “modern pageant glamour in the best way.”
Carter Gregory
Carter Gregory, vice president of A&R at Capitol Music Group, leaned fully into rock-and-roll glamour in archival Tom Ford.
“Carter Gregory wearing archival Tom Ford was peak rock and roll,” Gillette says. She points to the leather pants and leopard print as a particularly bold combination.
The unexpected color combination also kept the ensemble feeling contemporary. The black and brown, she says, “kept this look feeling fashion forward and modern.”
Teyana Taylor
Teyana Taylor knows how to make an entrance, and both fashion experts took notice.

Gillette called Taylor’s Zuhair Murad Couture look “gothic glam at its finest,” pointing to the crochet-inspired fabric, dramatic neckline and lush feather details. The result, she says, was “red carpet alchemy.”
DuRocher was equally enthusiastic about Taylor’s revealing gown.

“This is how you wear a revealing dress to an awards show, it’s provocative, but it still feels elegant,” she says. “I love the lace and beaded detailing and the way the look plays with coverage and skin.”
Nicky Hilton
DuRocher immediately noticed the rhinestones, sheer detailing and form-fitting silhouette.
“I especially love the detail in the back. The dress itself is a wow moment,” she says.
Lisa Rinna
Lisa Rinna brought a little ’80s glamour to the VMAs, and DuRocher was here for it.
“I love the white dress paired with her short, bleached hair, the entire look feels very ’80s in the best possible way,” she says.
It’s the cohesion of the styling that really works for her. “Everything works together, from the styling to the silhouette, and she looks completely put together,” DuRocher says.
Olandria Carthen
The “Love Island” star brought early-2000s pop-star energy to the VMAs in a lace-up MMS look.
“Olandria seemed to be channeling a pop star from the early aughts in this laced up MMS look that hit on both the textural and corseting trends we saw all over the red carpet tonight,” Gillette says.
She could even picture a certain pop icon in it: “I could absolutely see Christina Aguilera wearing something like this to the VMAs 25 years ago.”
Gillette also loved the way Carthen modernized the look with the red details and feminine bow at the hem, which played against the tougher leather.
Sienna Spiro
Sienna Spiro, who won the award for best new artist, caught DuRocher’s eye for an entirely different reason: intricate femininity.
“Sienna Spiro’s gown is so intricate and delicate,” she says. “I love the detailing throughout the dress and the way it feels incredibly feminine while still making an impact on the carpet.”
“The shape and embellishment give it a beautiful sense of glamour without feeling overdone,” DuRocher says.
Lisa
Lisa made a case for red and then doubled down with an oversized matching jacket.
“Lisa looks spectacular,” DuRocher says. “I love the red dress paired with that big, oversized red jacket, it feels bold, glamorous and incredibly current.”
She also sees the outfit as a snapshot of two major trends coming together. “Red is having such a moment right now, and so is lace, so I love seeing those trends come together here.”
Troye Sivan
Troye Sivan, the Australian singer, took a more unexpected approach in Erdem, and Gillette loved the contrast.

“The interplay between the masculine suit with the very high almost Edwardian collar against the draped silk and feathers is such a strong contrast especially since everything is in black and super crisp optic white,” she says.
Taylor Swift
“There’s something deliciously dark about this,” Paige says. “It’s almost ‘Practical Magic’ witchery, but rendered in liquid shimmer.”

The juxtaposition gives the look a sense of “sorceress” glamour, while the silver draping adds a touch of disco, she says. The asymmetry, Paige adds, keeps all that drama in Tamara Ralph’s couture collectionfeeling effortless rather than overworked.
Shaboozey

“Entirely rock star,” Paige says. “The leather three-piece could have gone costume very quickly, but the lean proportions, skinny tie, statement buckle and cropped trouser keep it feeling intentional rather than too theatrical.”

The combination gives the look an “outlaw-meets-frontman energy,” she says. The result feels polished without losing its edge, “like he might accept an award and then immediately disappear onto a tour bus.”

title: How Many VMAs Has Taylor Swift Won?
summary: How many VMAs does Taylor Swift have? She just set a record by winning 33.
story: Taylor Swift has a long history with the MTV VMAs and just broke yet another record.

Swift became the most awarded solo artist in VMAs history after the 2024 ceremony, at which she won seven total trophies. That brought her career total to 30, tying her with Beyoncé at the time.

title: ‘Zoolander’ Turns 25: Ben Stiller Promoted His Comedy on TODAY in 2001 After a Heavy Time for the Country
summary: In 2001, Ben Stiller spoke with TODAY about “Zoolander” coming out less than three weeks after the Sept. 11 terror attacks.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Ben Stiller, who stopped by the show on Sept. 28, 2001 to talk about his movie “Zoolander,” which came out in the wake of the Sept. 11 terror attacks.

Comedy was in an unprecedented situation of uncertainty after the events of Sept. 11. No one knew when, or if, the country would be ready to laugh again, as a reeling country continued to mourn the terror attacks. It was into this uncharted environment that Ben Stiller found himself when “Zoolander” was released in theaters on Sept. 28, 2001.

That same day, Stiller appeared on TODAY with Katie Couric, not just to talk about the film that poked fun at the modeling industry, but also the circumstances under which it would be served up to the public.
“You’re hoping to provide people with some much needed escapism,” Couric said.
“Yeah, just (a) distraction,” Stiller replied.

As it turned out, there was an appetite for comedy and Derek Zoolander’s famed “Blue Steel” gaze. The movie would open in second place, en route to a $45 million take at the domestic box office. The film eventually became a favorite in the Stiller canon and spawned a sequel in 2016.
What Did Ben Stiller Say About Releasing ‘Zoolander’ After 9/11?

“It’s a really strange time to just be talking about movies and entertainment because it just all kind of does seem frivolous,” he said. “For me, like having the movie come out now, the toughest thing about it. I thought it was a good idea to be able to have a comedy for people to go to if they wanted to, to have that option. But talking about it seems kind of not important.”
Stiller, who co-wrote, co-produced, starred in and directed “Zoolander,” called it a “really silly, ridiculous comedy” that he had seen since the attacks, but before it was officially released.

“Everything is different now,” he said. “But the great thing about seeing it, I’ve seen it with some audiences since this, and people are laughing. And it does seem to at least kind of be so silly that it kind of takes them out of stuff for awhile. But, definitely, everything’s different now.”
What Did Ben Stiller Think About Skewering the Fashion Industry?

When it came to poking fun at the fashion industry, Stiller said, “I can relate to it because we, in show business, I think sometimes take ourselves a little too seriously, get wrapped up in our own craziness.”
Adding, “In a way, it’s kind of like, working out some of those demons, not just kind of making fun of the modeling industry because that’s pretty easy.”
How Did ‘Zoolander’ Land So Many Celebrity Cameos?

“Zoolander” featured some serious star power in small roles. David Bowie, Lenny Kravitz, Winona Ryder, Gwen Stefani, Christian Slater, Donald Trump and Lance Bass are just some of the people who had cameos.
“Everybody kind of wanted to just have fun. It’s a real, like I said, it’s a silly movie, so they read the script and it just kind of felt like a fun thing to do,” Stiller said.

title: Adam Lambert Shocks Crowd With Surprise Performance During VMAs George Michael Tribute
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
story: Surprise!

The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
The homage comes a decade after the pop legend and queer icon died on Christmas Day 2016 at age 53.
Lambert, joined by several other artists including singer Meek and MNEK, belted out the 1990 hit. Several in the crowd were brought to their feet during the performance.

The tribute also featured Sombr, who performed Michael’s hit songs “Faith” and “Father Figure,” Raye, who performed “Knew You Were Waiting,” and Teddy Swims who sang a rendition of “Careless Whisper.”
During his portion, Sombr also wore a black Harley-Davidson jacket that originally worn by Michael during his 1988 Faith Tour, according to Vogue.
“To wear a jacket that has become so synonymous with that era was pretty surreal, and an honor,” Sombr told the magazine.

Michael, who won a host of VMAs, including the Video Vanguard lifetime achievement award in 1989, was highly regarded as a pioneering artist in the pop music scene, making a significant impact both as one-half of the duo Wham! and also as a solo artist.
While the icon was known for his many musical hits, he is also remembered as a champion of the LGBTQ+ community and philanthropist, who used his platform to help find a cure for HIV and AIDS.

Michael was outed as gay in 1998 following an incident in Beverly Hills during which he was arrested for engaging in a lewd act at a public toilet. Michael later roasted the ordeal in his music video for “Outside,” in which he mocked the Los Angeles police officers who caught him by featuring two uniformed officers kissing.

“I’m a very proud man. I want people to know that I have not been exposed as a gay man,” Michael told CNN in a now-famous 1998 interview. “I don’t feel any shame whatsoever, and neither do I think I should.”
With his unapologetic embrace of his sexuality, the musician is credited with opening the door and empowering many other queer entertainers in the music industry.

Given his rich legacy, many fans initially called out the VMAs for its choice in tribute performers — none of whom had publicly identified as a member of the LGBTQ+ community. MTV had announced exclusively in Rolling Stone Sept. 22 that acts Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims would be performing. Many felt that without performers who reflected Michael’s activism and identity, the LGBTQ community was being snubbed.

“You’d think with George being an icon for the LGBT community, they’d get someone like Sam Smith or Troye Sivan involved,” one user wrote on social media platform Reddit, referencing other openly gay pop icons.
While no other artists were announced ahead of the awards, singer Adam Lambert posted a cryptic Instagram story which featured Michael’s song “Freedom ‘90.”

title: A Brief History of Madonna and the VMAs, Going Back to 1984: ‘The House She Helped Build’
summary: Madonna is returning to the VMAs. What is Madonna’s history with the VMAs?
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Where would the MTV Video Music Awards be without Madonna?

Madonna’s name is practically synonymous with the VMAs. She was there from the beginning, rolling around the stage in a wedding dress while performing “Like A Virgin” during the awards show’s 1984 debut.

Over the next four decades, Madonna returned to the VMAs to deliver groundbreaking performances. She’s also made headlines with outrageous antics — like French kissing Britney Spears onstage — and touched fans’ hearts with an emotional tribute to Michael Jackson after the musician’s death in 2009.
Now, the Queen of Pop is poised make a historic return to the 2026 VMAs on Sept. 27 when she performs at the awards show for the first time in 23 years.
Madonna’s performance will kick off the awards show for a record-breaking fifth time, ending her tie with Rihanna, who’s opened the show four times.
Madonna who released her hit album, “Confessions II,” in July, also goes into this year’s VMAs as the most nominated performer.
The singer is “returning to sit on her throne for the night,” NBC News entertainment contributor Chris Witherspoon tells TODAY.com.

“You simply cannot tell the story of the VMAs without telling the story of Madonna. From ‘Like a Virgin’ in 1984, to ‘Vogue’ in 1990, to that unforgettable 2003 performance with Britney Spears, Christina Aguilera and Missy Elliott, Madonna understood the assignment before we even had the phrase,” said Witherspoon.
“Madonna returning to the VMAs doesn’t feel like a comeback to me. It feels like the Queen of Pop returning to the house she helped build,” Witherspoon added.
Ahead of Madonna’s triumphant VMAs return, let’s take a look back at her 10 biggest moments at the awards show.
1) The Wedding Dress Seen Round the World (1984)

Madonna’s audacious performance at the inaugural MTV Video Music Awards in 1984 — she rolled around the stage in a punky ensemble that includes a wedding dress, rosary beads and a “Boy Toy” belt buckle — became her breakout moment.
The raunchy performance, which also included some bumping and grinding, also branded the VMAs as a rebellious alternative to the Grammys and other awards shows.

“MTV could barely fill the seats at the VMAs in year one. By year two, pretty much every act wanted a spot on that stage. Madonna was at the first show in 1984, rolling across the stage in a wedding dress singing ‘Like a Virgin.’ I’d give her a lot of credit for that turnaround,” Jeff Moore, a music marketing strategist, professor, and former touring musician, told TODAY.com.
2) Madonna Expresses Herself (1989)
Madonna returned to the VMAs five years later to deliver one of her finest televised performances when she sang “Express Yourself” with her two backup singers-dancers.

The newly divorced singer — her marriage to Sean Penn officially ended earlier in the year —  began her high-energy, tightly choreographed performance wearing a dark suit before stripping down to a corset.
3) ‘Vogue’ Meets the French Revolution (1990)

The former Material Girl’s breathtaking 1990 performance of “Vogue” was inspired by the French Revolution. Madge as Marie Antoinette? Oh, it worked, right down to her and her dancers’ 18th century-style powdered wigs, heavy white face makeup and corseted gowns.
4) ‘Ray of Light’ with Lenny Kravtiz (1998)
In what’s considered one of the best live performances, Madonna showed off her vocal chops on the soaring “Ray of Light’ with guest guitarist Lenny Kravitz during the 1998 show.
The singer, who kicked off the performance with the Hindu-inspired  “Shanti Ashtangi,” also swept the awards that night, taking home five Moon Man trophies.
5) Madonna Meets Her Drag Impersonators (1999)
The singer was feted the following year by a group of drag queens who wore some of her most memorable looks as they lip-synched and danced to her greatest hits.
“All I have to say is that it takes a real man to fill my shoes!” the singer quipped afterwards.
6) Kissing Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera (2003)
In 2003, Madonna shocked viewers when she took a moment during a throwback performance of “Like A Virgin” to kiss shared her guest performers Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.
Spears and Aguilera donned skimpy wedding dress looks in a fun nod to Madonna’s debut VMAs performance.
7) An Emotional Tribute to Michael Jackson (2009)

Madonna showed off her serious side when she paid an emotional tribute to her late fellow pop icon Michael Jackson at the 2009 VMAs, calling Jackson “one of the greatest talents the world has ever known.”

“His music,” she said in her speech, “had an extra layer of inexplicable magic that didn’t just make you want to dance but actually made you believe you could fly, dare to dream, be anything that you wanted to be.”
She also recalled going to dinner with Jackson years before.

“Later we went back to my house to watch a movie and sat on the couch like two kids, and somewhere in the middle of the movie, his hand snuck over and held mine,” she said. “It felt like he was looking for more of a friend than a romance, and I was happy to oblige. In that moment, he didn’t feel like a superstar. He felt like a human being.”
8) A Surprise Appearance, Motherf-----! (2021)
Decked out out black dominatrix bodysuit and cap, Madonna made a surprise appearance to open the 2021 VMAs.
The singer’s appearance came just after viewers watched a short video telling the story of her arrival in New York City decades before with just $35 to her name.
Madonna then walked out onstage, telling the crowd, “And they said we wouldn’t last. But we’re still here, motherf------!”

title: Taylor Swift Reflects on Her 60 Music Videos While Accepting the Inaugural Artist Director Honors at the VMAs
summary: What did Taylor Swift say in her speech while accepting the inaugural Artist Director Honors at the 2026 VMAs?
story: Taylor Swift already has 30 VMAs. At the 2026 ceremony, she racked up another honor, and she was the first to ever receive it: the Artist Director Honors.
The pop icon was presented the award by friend Dakota Johnson, who celebrated the “visionary with a relentless drive for perfection for everything she does.”

Viewers and the audience then watched a clip of behind-the-scenes of Swift bringing the ideas to the screen. Swift talked through her thought process and said, “I think I will always want to tell human stories about human emotion.”
In her speech during the ceremony on Sept. 27, she reflected on making “roughly” 60 music videos throughout her decades-long career, including 18 that she wrote and directed.

“I’ve got to tell you though the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun,” she said as the crowd erupted into cheers and applause.
She said she finds the experience “so rewarding” before thanking every person who has contributed to her music videos, adding that she learned something from all of them.
Swift concluded her speech by again expressing her gratitude for his fans before unveiling her latest masterpiece: the music video for new single “Patient Zero.”

The VMAs previously shared in a press release that the special honor was created to recognize “groundbreaking music artists whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling.”
Swift had an eventful evening. The awards show came two days after she released four new songs as part of her “The Life of the Showgirl: The Encore” album.
The music video for one of the new songs, “Patient Zero,” debuted at the VMAs after her speech.
She proudly watched the clip with Johnson, who starred in the music video, by her side.

title: British police find no explosives in vehicles of men detained near base used by U.S.
summary: No explosives were found in vehicles searched after five men were arrested in connection with a huge security operation near an air base used by the U.S.
story: No explosives were found in vehicles searched after five men were arrested in connection with a huge security operation near an air base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, British counter terror police confirmed Tuesday.

In an update explaining Monday’s decision to bail all five suspects who were arrested on terror and explosives charges, Laurence Taylor, Britain’s head of counter terror policing, said “a quantity” of gasoline was recovered from three vans near RAF Fairford.

“Those vehicles have been subject to extensive examination, with the support of military assets and forensic experts, and we can confirm that no improvised explosive devices were found,” he said, adding that investigators had searched properties in London.
Taylor said it was an “investigative decision” to release the men on bail, “grounded in experience and careful considerations of policing powers.”
No charges have been filed against the men.

Taylor’s comments came after President Donald Trump said he was surprised about that decision. “I would have said, ‘Don’t let them have bail,’” Trump said in the Oval Office on Monday. “I’m surprised that they released them, I wouldn’t have done that.”

title: Iran ‘fully prepared’ for war to resume but diplomacy not over yet, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says
summary: Despite Trump’s comments rejecting a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said Iran hadn’t yet officially responded to the proposal.
story: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said his country is prepared to resume fighting with the United States but has not yet abandoned diplomacy after President Donald Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

“We are fully prepared for the time for the war to be resumed, and I repeat, we stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war,” Araghchi told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday, when asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Trump could seek to resume bombing after the U.S. midterm elections. “At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”

Iran had offered a deal last week to reopen the strait and resume normal maritime passage through the critical global oil chokepoint within seven days, as part of a plan conveyed to the U.S. through mediator Qatar on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Trump said Saturday that he had turned down that proposal, telling reporters: “I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly.”
Araghchi told moderator Kristen Welker on Sunday that despite Trump’s public comments, the rejection had still not been officially communicated to Iran via mediators.

He reaffirmed that Iran was ready to reopen the strait as part of an agreement to end the conflict, adding that in return, “we want our monies, our assets, which are illegally frozen, to be released. We want to be able to sell our oil.”

Araghchi said the conditions were “not new” and were things the U.S. has already committed itself to previously, referring to the memorandum of understanding that the two countries signed in June that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. That agreement collapsed within days after fresh strikes were exchanged.
“If you ask us, there is no reason why we should go back to diplomacy,” Araghchi said. “But I am still trying diplomacy because I think we shouldn’t miss any chance for peace.”
“We don’t care about U.S. midterm elections,” the Iranian official added. “We care about our national interests.”

Prior to Araghchi’s interview, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told “Meet the Press” that the deal was rejected for “a number of reasons,” suggesting the U.S. could not permit Iran “to have access to billions in frozen funds.”

Waltz said: “I think this was a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable, to ask for the release of the blockade, the sanctions, international sanctions and access to billions in assets.”
He also questioned “who’s calling the shots in Iran right now,” adding that the country had violated the past memorandum of understanding by attacking international shipping.

“I think it’s kind of common sense that the president doesn’t have a lot of confidence this time after we just tried a few months ago,” Waltz added. “What I can tell you is the president will leave all options on the table to ensure the world is safe from Iran holding the world hostage with a nuclear weapon.”
Asked what deal Trump would accept, Waltz said: “I’m not going to negotiate for the president.”
“This is about keeping the next generation safe from Iran threatening the world with a nuclear weapon,” he added.
Trump said last week he was still considering whether to “annihilate” Iran or make a deal.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November midterms. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.

title: Trump says he has rejected Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
summary: Despite Trump’s comments, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said no rejection had come through official channels.
story: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after Iranian officials indicated that shipping through the critical waterway could resume within days if a deal was sealed.

“I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump told reporters as he boarded Marine One on the White House lawn, after indirect talks between the two countries were held on the sidelines of this week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York.

“What they wanted is to immediately open the Hormuz Strait. You know why? Because they’re dying. You know why they’re dying? Because they have no money coming in because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait,” he continued. “They outsmarted themselves. They said, ‘Let’s close it and cause a problem for the world.’ And I came along, and we put up the greatest blockade ever in military history.”
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected Iran’s offer to revive a ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a statement Saturday that no rejection had come through official channels.
“We saw the first reaction from the President of America, but nothing has yet been conveyed to us from the mediators,” he said in a statement.

He added: “Of course, the President of America has also made many good remarks as well as many contradictory remarks, which unfortunately we hear from him frequently. We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us and we will make a decision based on that.”
On Friday, Araghchi had told reporters Hormuz “can be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days” if Iran’s conditions were met.
He said a “concrete seven-day plan” that includes reopening the strait had been conveyed to the U.S. through mediator Qatar and was ready to start “as soon as the United States accepts this plan.”
Iran offers new proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz

Araghchi said the actions required of the U.S. in Iran’s proposal were commitments already agreed to in the June memorandum of understanding between the two countries that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. That agreement, signed in June, collapsed within days after fresh strikes were exchanged.
One of the conditions of the plan is for the U.S. to accept a maritime transit route through the Strait of Hormuz that has been agreed upon by Iran and Oman, Araghchi had said Thursday.
A U.S. official said on Friday that the Trump administration was having positive and constructive discussions through the mediators but that it was not in any hurry to reach an agreement.

“The United States is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz, so we are not in a rush,” the U.S. official said. “Over the last 48 hours, nearly 40 million barrels of oil have transited the strait.”

Earlier this week, Trump said he was still considering whether to “annihilate” Iran or make a deal. Early Saturday, he posted an image to Truth Social of the Strait of Hormuz labeled the “Trump Strait.”

In an interview with Al Jazeera on Saturday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that resolving the Hormuz issue “is possible through negotiations, not the use of force,” but warned that his country does not “trust” talks with Washington.

Trump has repeatedly said that the goal of attacking Iran was to prevent the development of a nuclear weapon. Soon after the war started, Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the conflict, sending shock waves through the world economy.
Pezeshkian on Thursday suggested his government was willing to make a deal with the U.S. to end the war before Americans head to the polls this November.

“We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian said in a brief meeting with NBC News and other news organizations, two days after Trump said he believed the Iranian regime would not make a deal to settle the conflict until after the elections.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November midterms. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.
The U.S. this week announced it would impose sanctions on any global companies doing business ​with Iranian airlines, with the aim of grounding Iran’s entire civil fleet worldwide.

Iraq said Saturday that it was engaging with the U.S. in an effort to restore humanitarian flights to and from Iran, after Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries in response to the sanctions.

Efforts were ongoing to “secure exemptions for certain Iraqi airports from these measures” in order to enable “the resumption of flights for humanitarian reasons, such as medical treatment, education, religious pilgrimages, and the interests of civilians,” the Iraqi prime minister’s office said.
Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that flights had also been shut down to Oman, Georgia and Azerbaijan.

title: Iran’s president says Tehran wants a deal with U.S. before midterm elections
summary: In an exchange with news organizations, Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian also described meeting twice with the Islamic Republic’s new supreme leader, who hasn’t been seen in public.
story: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday suggested his government was willing to make a deal with the U.S. to end the war before Americans head to the polls this November.
“We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian said in a brief meeting with NBC News and other news organizations on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

“We wish Americans to return to the MOU before the midterms,” Pezeshkian added, referring to a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. The agreement, signed in June, eventually collapsed.
Iran’s president strikes a defiant tone at U.N. after Trump threats

In response to NBC News’ request for comment, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said: “The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region.”
“The President is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable,” Kelly added.

Pezeshkian’s comments came two days after President Donald Trump said in a speech to world leaders at the U.N. that he believed the Iranian regime would not make a deal to settle the conflict until after the fall elections.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November contests. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told a group of reporters in a separate briefing in New York on Thursday that a plan has been presented to U.S. officials through mediators during talks this week that would lead to the opening of the Strait of Hormuz and the resumption of talks after seven days.
Araghchi said the plan could begin as soon as the U.S. agreed to it and maintained it plan did not go beyond the memorandum of understanding signed by Trump in June.

“We have introduced a plan to the United States through the intermediators that, if certain conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will be open at the end of seven days and talks will be restarted,” Araghchi said. “The conditions we have asked the U.S. to meet is nothing new, nothing more than what was already in the Islamabad agreement, which was signed by the U.S. president.”
Araghchi pointed out that one of the conditions of the plan is for the U.S. to accept a maritime transit route through the Strait of Hormuz that has been agreed upon by Iran and Oman.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump on Tuesday defended the conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country or make a deal.

Trump has repeatedly said that the goal of attacking Iran was to prevent the development of a nuclear weapon. Soon after the war started, Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the conflict, sending shock waves through the world economy.
In the exchange with news organizations, Pezeshkian said he has met with the Islamic Republic’s new leader twice — including a month ago, for seven hours.

Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei assumed the role in early March after his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in an Israeli attack that also killed family members and other senior leaders.

Pezeshkian said he did not see “any issues with his health or physical appearance” in their meetings, adding that they sat on the floor on traditional pillows. Mojtaba Khamenei was severely injured in the strike that killed his father, three people with knowledge of the matter told NBC News in July, with burns to his face and body and wounds that have required several operations to one of his legs.

Iran’s president briefly addressed other pressing issues affecting the relationship between Tehran and Washington. He said his government was “open” to inspections of its nuclear facilities, which the regime has long maintained are for civilian purposes, and he insisted the regime was not seeking to assassinate the American president.
“This has not been the position of the Iranian government that we seek to assassinate President Trump or his family members,” Pezeshkian said.
